technical: The time and cost claim is stronger than the evidence. RUN minutes=20.3 most likely covers the scripted run, not the full span from terraform apply to destroy, and the README budgets about an hour. Fix: Quote the logged wall-clock time for each phase from the run (apply, reproduce, fix, destroy). If those timings aren't logged, say 'plan for about an hour, as the README does' and drop the per-step minute counts that weren't measured.

The headline numbers match corroborated contract results. 400 of 400 messages share a trace (05-fix.log:37). The header root matches the producer span (05-fix.log:50). 10 of 10 sampled traces hold both services in Splunk (05-fix.log:91). The map path is at 05-fix.log:85.

The controls are real and the before-check could have failed. The no-agent run checks for a header on the probe message. The jar hash is compared between runs. The agent version is pinned and checked, and its effective settings are printed. Receive spans are counted as a positive control, going from 0 to 76.
The repo link and the clone path in the post point to a different path from the published lab URL, so a reader may not be able to reproduce the run as written.

The '20 minutes from terraform apply through destroy' figure is not backed by shown timings. The README budgets an hour, and creating an EKS control plane alone usually takes longer than the 8 minutes claimed for Step 1.
The reader and the decision are clear, and the opening delivers its promise in the first sentence with a real count.

It adds something beyond the docs. There is a per-message join on a real queue, the header trace ID is shown next to the producer span, and the post shows that with receive telemetry the link sits on the process span, not the receive span. It also explains why 100 messages produced 76 receive spans. Even so, the core finding confirms a default the maintainer already describes.
The span_tree output that backs 'one receive span held two process spans, each with its own link' is described but not shown. Paste that tree. It is the most original evidence in the post.

Mounting the agent jar with hostPath is presented as what you'd ship. Add one line pointing production readers to an init container or the OpenTelemetry Operator for injection. Also note in the opening that a Collector (the Splunk OTel Collector here) must be reachable, not only the one variable.
There is no search-volume data. The only signal is one GitHub discussion (#14193) with 5 comments and 15 replies and a follow-up question in June 2026. The brief rates that as weak.
The title uses the words a searcher would use (SQS, Java agent, Splunk APM, zero code) and credits the products with the answer. Without stronger demand evidence it cannot score above 3.
Splunk fits naturally: the service map with the inferred sqs node and the trace lookup are the reader's payoff, not decoration.

claims.text: The AWSTraceHeader system attribute doesn't count towards message size.
AWSTraceHeader holds a header in AWS X-Ray format.
The Java instrumentation uses AWSTraceHeader by default to carry context.
A maintainer says producer and consumer should share a trace by default.
otel.instrumentation.aws-sdk.experimental-use-propagator-for-messaging defaults to false, and turning it on moves context into message attributes with the configured propagator.
The maintainer says the propagator setting changes how context travels, not whether spans share a trace, and suggests it for a stand-in that doesn't keep AWSTraceHeader.
The maintainer discussion notes exceptions for batch receives.
The receive telemetry setting is experimental and off by default at v2.33.1.
The whole lab takes about 20 minutes from terraform apply through terraform destroy, including about 8 minutes for Step 1.
100 messages made 76 receive spans because one poll can return several messages.
Teams using SqsTemplate and single-message @SqsListener methods can roll out the agent before asking for code changes, generalised beyond this one lab setup.

brief.reader: Platform engineer running Spring Boot services on EKS that talk over Amazon SQS
brief.decision: Whether to roll out the OTel Java agent alone for queue tracing, before asking any team for code changes or extra settings
brief.question: With only the Java agent attached, do my SQS producer and consumer land in one trace, and do I need a setting for that?
brief.takeaway: You can follow a message across SQS in Splunk APM from one environment variable, on the OpenTelemetry Java agent's defaults, and you know the one setting that gives each consumer a linked trace of its own.
brief.adds: Existing pages name the settings and describe the system attribute. This post counts real messages on a real queue, shows the header on a waiting message next to the producer span's trace ID, and measures what one setting changes.
brief.open_question: Of 400 messages sent through a real SQS queue with the Java agent on its defaults, what percent have producer and process spans sharing one trace ID, and with receive telemetry on, how many of 100 stay in that trace and how many link to it?
tradeoffs: One trace per message by default, or receive telemetry with each consumer in a linked trace of its own
The AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, or the configured propagator in message attributes

existing_pages.title: Springboot sqs instrumentation
existing_pages.covers: A maintainer explains that context travels in the AWSTraceHeader system attribute by default, that producer and consumer should share a trace by default, and that receive telemetry gives separate traces joined by a span link. It gives no per-message count on real SQS.

existing_pages.title: Message metadata for Amazon SQS
existing_pages.covers: Message system attributes, and AWSTraceHeader as the supported one, holding an X-Ray trace header string. It doesn't cover the Java agent.

existing_pages.title: Settings for the AWS SDK instrumentation
existing_pages.covers: The agent's AWS SDK settings and their defaults, including the propagator setting for SNS and SQS, which defaults to false.

existing_pages.title: AWS SDK instrumentation metadata, v2.33.1
existing_pages.covers: The instrumentation's settings at v2.33.1, including receive telemetry, off by default, which starts a new consumer trace with a span link to the producer.

existing_pages.title: Spring Cloud AWS
existing_pages.covers: How to send with SqsTemplate and receive with SqsListener, with its own Observability Support section.
